question: What is the maximum statutory timeframe in hours for a data controller to notify a personal data breach to the supervisory authority under Article 33?
ground_truth: The controller must notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 33(1) (Page 52)[cite: 2]

question: What is the maximum administrative fine under Article 83(5) for infringements of the basic principles for processing?
ground_truth: Infringements are subject to administrative fines up to 20 000 000 EUR, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 4% of the total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 83(5) (Pages 82-83)[cite: 2]

question: Under Article 8(1), what is the default age threshold below which processing the data of a child for information society services requires parental authorization?
ground_truth: Processing is lawful where the child is at least 16 years old; below 16 years, consent must be given or authorized by the holder of parental responsibility[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 8(1) (Page 37)[cite: 2]

question: What is the minimum duration for the term of office of members of each supervisory authority specified in Article 54?
ground_truth: The duration of the term of the member or members of each supervisory authority must be no less than four years[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 54(1)(d) (Page 67)[cite: 2]

question: What is the standard temporal deadline for an organization to furnish an initial substantive reply to an individual exercising their statutory privacy entitlements?
ground_truth: The controller shall provide information on action taken on a request to the data subject without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 12(3) (Page 40)[cite: 2]

question: Below what employee headcount threshold is an enterprise generally exempt from maintaining records of processing activities?
ground_truth: The record-keeping obligations do not apply to an enterprise or organisation employing fewer than 250 persons, unless specific high-risk, non-occasional, or sensitive processing conditions are met[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 30(5) (Page 51)[cite: 2]

question: What is the maximum duration for which a formal data protection seal or compliance credential can be conferred before requiring reassessment?
ground_truth: Certification shall be issued to a controller or processor for a maximum period of three years and may be renewed under the same conditions[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 42(7) (Page 59)[cite: 2]

question: Why can a data controller refuse to fulfill an individual's right to erasure even when the person has revoked their explicit consent under Article 17?
ground_truth: Under Article 17(1)(b) and 17(3), erasure upon withdrawal of consent does not apply if there is another legal ground for processing, or to the extent that processing remains necessary for exercising the right of freedom of expression and information, complying with a legal obligation, public health reasons, public interest archiving/research, or the establishment, exercise, or defence of legal claims[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 17(1)(b), Article 17(3) (Pages 43-44)[cite: 2]

question: What causes the lead supervisory authority to refer a cross-border draft decision to the European Data Protection Board for binding dispute settlement?
ground_truth: Under Article 60(4) and Article 65(1)(a), referral occurs when a supervisory authority concerned raises a relevant and reasoned objection to the lead authority's draft decision within four weeks, and the lead supervisory authority either rejects the objection as not being relevant or reasoned, or chooses not to follow it[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 60(4), Article 65(1)(a) (Pages 71, 74-75)[cite: 2]

question: Compare the statutory penalty tiers under Article 83(4) and Article 83(5) regarding fine ceilings and the underlying categories of legal violations.
ground_truth: Article 83(4) imposes fines up to 10 000 000 EUR or 2% of total worldwide annual turnover for procedural and technical violations (such as controller/processor obligations in Articles 8, 11, 25-39, 42, and 43), whereas Article 83(5) imposes higher fines up to 20 000 000 EUR or 4% of worldwide turnover for core infringements of basic processing principles (Articles 5, 6, 7, 9), data subjects' rights (Articles 12-22), cross-border transfers (Articles 44-49), and non-compliance with supervisory orders[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 83(4), Article 83(5) (Pages 82-83)[cite: 2]

question: How do the mandatory transparency disclosures under Article 13 differ from those under Article 14 in terms of timing and disclosure of the origin of data?
ground_truth: Under Article 13 (data collected directly from the data subject), information must be provided at the time when data are obtained and does not require disclosing external sources[cite: 2]. Under Article 14 (data not obtained from the data subject), information must be provided within a reasonable period (at latest one month, or upon first communication/disclosure) and must explicitly specify the categories of data and from which source the personal data originate, including whether they came from publicly accessible sources[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 13(1), Article 14(1)-(3) (Pages 40-42)[cite: 2]

question: What sequential procedural stages must the lead supervisory authority follow under Article 60 when cooperating with other concerned authorities on a draft decision?
ground_truth: First, the lead authority communicates relevant information and submits a draft decision without delay; second, concerned authorities have four weeks to express relevant and reasoned objections; third, if an objection is followed, the lead submits a revised draft subject to objection within two weeks; fourth, if no objection is raised or agreement is reached, the lead adopts and notifies the decision to the main establishment and informs other authorities and the Board[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 60(3)-(7) (Page 71)[cite: 2]

question: What sequence of mandatory analytical steps must a controller follow when carrying out a Data Protection Impact Assessment under Article 35?
ground_truth: The controller must seek the advice of the data protection officer (where designated); compile a systematic description of envisaged processing operations and purposes; assess the necessity and proportionality of the processing; assess the specific risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects; and detail the safeguards and security measures envisaged to address those risks[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 35(2), Article 35(7) (Pages 53-54)[cite: 2]

question: Under Article 33(2), a data processor is legally obligated to notify data breaches directly to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours, correct?
ground_truth: No, under Article 33(2), the processor shall notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach, whereas the obligation to notify the supervisory authority rests on the controller under Article 33(1)[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 33(1)-(2) (Page 52)[cite: 2]

question: Article 8 mandates that across all European Union Member States, the age of consent for information society services must remain strictly fixed at 18 years without exception, right?
ground_truth: No, Article 8(1) sets the default age at 16 years, and explicitly permits Member States to provide by law for a lower age provided that it is not below 13 years[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 8(1) (Page 37)[cite: 2]

question: Since the right to data portability under Article 20 is absolute, an individual is legally entitled to extract proprietary corporate source code and colleague records, correct?
ground_truth: No, Article 20 applies only to personal data concerning the data subject that they have provided to a controller based on consent or contract, and Article 20(4) explicitly specifies that the right to data portability shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others[cite: 2].
source_reference: Article 20(1), Article 20(4) (Page 45)[cite: 2]

question: On what date did the Law on the Protection of Personal Data No. 6698 come into force upon its publication in the Official Gazette?
ground_truth: Law No. 6698 came into force after its publication in the Official Gazette No. 29677 on 7 April 2016[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Data Protection in Turkey (Page 4)[cite: 3]

question: Within what deadline must a data controller send documents requested by the Board during an official investigation?
ground_truth: The controller shall send the information and documents demanded by the Board related to the subject of examination within fifteen days[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Right to Lodge a Complaint (Page 23)[cite: 3]

question: Within how many days must a data controller implement a decision issued by the Board to remedy identified infringements?
ground_truth: The decision shall be implemented without delay and within thirty days at the latest after the notification[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Right to Lodge a Complaint & Obligation to Fulfil Board Decisions (Pages 23, 35)[cite: 3]

question: According to the By-Law mentioned in Law No. 6698, what is the mandatory minimum period for storing records of data disposal operations?
ground_truth: All operations relating to erasure, destruction, and anonymisation of personal data shall be recorded and stored for a minimum of three years[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Erasure, Destruction or Anonymisation of Personal Data (Page 28)[cite: 3]

question: What fee per sheet may be charged to an applicant when a controller provides a physical paper reply extending beyond ten pages?
ground_truth: No fee will be charged up to ten pages, and 1 Turkish Lira may be charged per page over ten pages[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Obligation to Respond to the Request of Data Subject (Page 34)[cite: 3]

question: Within what period must a data controller update the public register after alterations occur in its VERBİS filings?
ground_truth: In case of any change in the Registry records, data controllers shall notify the Authority through VERBİS within seven days of the date of change[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Obligation to Register to Data Controllers' Registry (Page 32)[cite: 3]

question: If the supervisory authority does not issue a determination regarding a formal citizen grievance, after how many days is the demand legally considered rejected?
ground_truth: In case the request is not responded to in sixty days from the date of complaint, the demand shall be deemed refused[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Right to Lodge a Complaint (Page 22)[cite: 3]

question: Why does a data controller violate the general principles of lawfulness and fairness if it continues processing data under other statutory bases after consent is withdrawn, when consent was improperly demanded?
ground_truth: Obtaining explicit consent when other legal processing conditions already exist is misleading and deemed a violation of rights; consequently, if the data subject withdraws that explicit consent, continuing to process the data under an alternative legal basis constitutes a violation of the rule of lawfulness and fairness[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Conditions for Personal Data Processing (Page 12)[cite: 3]

question: Under what statutory circumstances may the Personal Data Protection Board order the immediate cessation of data processing or cross-border data transfer under Article 15?
ground_truth: The Board may decide that processing of data or its transfer abroad should be stopped if such operation is clearly unlawful and may lead to damages that are difficult or impossible to compensate for[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Right to Lodge a Complaint (Page 23)[cite: 3]

question: Compare the processing conditions for personal data relating to health and sexual life against other special categories of personal data under Law No. 6698.
ground_truth: Special categories other than health and sexual life may be processed without explicit consent in cases provided for by laws[cite: 3]. In contrast, personal data concerning health and sexual life may only be processed without explicit consent by persons subject to a secrecy obligation or competent public institutions for public health, preventive medicine, medical diagnosis, treatment and care services, and planning, management, and financing of health-care services[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Conditions for Special Categories of Personal Data (Page 13)[cite: 3]

question: How do the definitions and operational scopes of erasure, destruction, and anonymisation differ under the KVKK framework?
ground_truth: Erasure renders personal data inaccessible and non-reusable specifically for the users concerned; destruction renders data inaccessible, irretrievable, and non-reusable by anyone by any means; and anonymisation renders data impossible to link with an identified or identifiable natural person even if matched with other data[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Erasure, Destruction or Anonymisation of Personal Data (Page 27)[cite: 3]

question: What mandatory procedural steps and timelines must an individual observe before properly submitting an official complaint to the Board under Article 13 and 14?
ground_truth: First, the data subject must submit their request directly to the data controller in writing or via recognized electronic methods[cite: 3]. The controller has up to thirty days to respond[cite: 3]. Only after exhausting this remedy—if the request is refused, found insufficient, or unanswered—may the individual lodge a complaint with the Board within thirty days of learning the response, or within sixty days of the initial application date in any case[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Rights of the Data Subject & Right to Lodge a Complaint (Pages 21-22, 34)[cite: 3]

question: What sequence of notifications and actions must a data controller take under Article 12 upon discovering that processed data has been unlawfully acquired by third parties?
ground_truth: In the event of an unlawful breach, the data controller must communicate the breach to the data subject and notify the Personal Data Protection Board within the shortest time[cite: 3]. If deemed necessary, the Board may subsequently announce the breach on its official website or through other methods[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Data Security Requirements (Page 30)[cite: 3]

question: Under Law No. 6698, a data controller can validly secure explicit consent using blanket statements covering 'all types of banking, commercial, and data processing activities', correct?
ground_truth: No, explicit consent must relate to a specified issue, be based on information, and be declared by free will; consent statements covering unspecified commercial or processing activities are blanket consents and are deemed legally invalid[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Key Points on Explicit Consent (Pages 14-15)[cite: 3]

question: Under Turkish data privacy law, an aggrieved data subject can bypass the data controller and lodge an immediate complaint with the Board directly, right?
ground_truth: No, the data subject must first make a request to the data controller; the Law expressly states that the data subject shall not contact the Board before exhausting the remedy of the request to the data controller[cite: 3].
source_reference: Section: Right to Lodge a Complaint (Page 22)[cite: 3]

question: Under Law No. 6698, data and proprietary business records of corporate legal entities receive the same direct legal protection as personal data of natural persons, correct?
ground_truth: No, only data of natural persons are protected under the Law; the Law does not regulate the protection of data concerning legal persons[cite: 3].

question: In what year of the Third Age did the Fallohide brothers Marcho and Blanco set out from Bree to cross the river Baranduin?

question: In what approximate year according to Shire calendar records did Tobold Hornblower pioneer the cultivation of genuine pipe-herb in his garden?

question: Why did Bilbo organize his lavish 111th birthday party with elaborate gift giveaways, and what was its underlying psychological purpose regarding the ring?
ground_truth: Bilbo explained to Gandalf that the party was intended to have his joke and give away lots of birthday presents, but its real purpose was to make it easier for him to give away the One Ring at the same time and permanently leave the Shire[cite: 4].
source_reference: Chapter 1: A Long-expected Party (Pages 42, 45)[cite: 4]

question: Why did Gandalf become alarmed during his private conversation with Bilbo after the party, and what warning did he subsequently give Frodo about the ring?
ground_truth: Gandalf became alarmed when Bilbo grew angry, hesitated to leave the ring, and called it 'my Precious' just as Gollum had[cite: 4]. Consequently, Gandalf warned Frodo that the magic ring might have powers beyond making the wearer vanish, strictly advising him to use it seldom or not at all, to avoid suspicion, and to keep it safe and secret[cite: 4].
source_reference: Chapter 1: A Long-expected Party (Pages 44, 47, 53)[cite: 4]

question: Compare the physical characteristics, lifestyle habits, and geographical preferences of the Harfoots, Stoors, and Fallohides.
ground_truth: Harfoots were browner of skin, smaller, shorter, beardless, preferred highlands and hillsides, had much to do with Dwarves, and lived in tunnels[cite: 4]. Stoors were broader, heavier-built, with larger hands and feet, grew down on their chins, were less shy of Men, and preferred flat lands and riversides[cite: 4]. Fallohides were fairer in skin and hair, taller, slimmer, lovers of trees and woodlands, skilled in language and song, and friendly with Elves[cite: 4].
source_reference: Prologue: Concerning Hobbits (Pages 4, 8)[cite: 4]

question: How did Bilbo's original invented tale about acquiring the ring from Gollum differ from the true account he later confessed to Gandalf?
ground_truth: In his original story to his companions, Bilbo claimed Gollum promised him a magic birthday ring if he won the riddle game and showed him the way out as a reward when the present went missing[cite: 4]. In the true account, Bilbo found the ring lying on the tunnel floor before meeting Gollum, won the game when asking what was in his pocket, and escaped when Gollum returned to fetch his ring to murder him[cite: 4].
source_reference: Prologue: Of the Finding of the Ring (Pages 14-17)[cite: 4]

question: Describe the sequential events from the conclusion of Bilbo's birthday speech to his departure from Bag End into the night.
ground_truth: Bilbo shouted his farewell announcement, slipped the ring onto his finger, and vanished in a blinding flash[cite: 4]; he walked back unseen to Bag End, changed out of party clothes into travel attire, and packed his belongings[cite: 4]; he placed the ring in an envelope for Frodo, argued with and conceded to Gandalf to leave it on the mantelpiece, met three dwarves outside, sang a walking song, and walked down into the meadows[cite: 4].
source_reference: Chapter 1: A Long-expected Party (Pages 40-47)[cite: 4]

question: What sequence of events led to the crossing of the Baranduin and the establishment of the Shire-reckoning calendar?

question: What anatomical landmark marks the exact border where retinal axons change their name from optic nerve to optic tract?
ground_truth: The optic chiasm is the specific place where the name changes from the optic nerve in the PNS to the optic tract in the CNS[cite: 5].

question: Which glial cells function as resident macrophages in the central nervous system to ingest pathogens and damaged tissue?
ground_truth: Microglia function as CNS-resident macrophages, performing immune surveillance and phagocytosis[cite: 5].

question: What specialized structure in the brain ventricles contacts ependymal cells with blood vessels to filter blood and generate cerebrospinal fluid?
ground_truth: The choroid plexus is the specialized structure in the ventricles where ependymal cells filter and absorb components of the blood to produce cerebrospinal fluid[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.2 Glial Cells of the CNS (Page 479)[cite: 5]

question: In which two specific anatomical regions are bipolar neurons primarily found in humans?
ground_truth: Bipolar cells are found mainly in the olfactory epithelium and as part of the retina[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.2 Types of Neurons (Page 476)[cite: 5]

question: What functional zone of a neuron, formed by the junction of the soma's base and the initial segment, generates nerve impulses?
ground_truth: Action potentials are generated in the trigger zone, which is a combination of the axon hillock and the initial segment[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.2 Parts of a Neuron (Page 475)[cite: 5]

question: Which peripheral supporting cells enclose and protect clusters of neuronal somas in sensory and autonomic ganglia?
ground_truth: Satellite cells surround the cell bodies of neurons in sensory and autonomic ganglia[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.2 Glial Cells of the PNS (Page 479)[cite: 5]

question: What structural term identifies the exposed unmyelinated spaces between consecutive glial wraps along an axon shaft?
ground_truth: Each gap in the myelin covering of an axon is called a node of Ranvier[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.2 Parts of a Neuron (Page 475)[cite: 5]

question: Why does an autoimmune attack in Multiple Sclerosis lead to tissue scarring, and how does this alteration affect neural transmission?
ground_truth: Antibodies produced by lymphocytes target myelin as foreign, initiating inflammation and myelin destruction in the CNS[cite: 5]; as the insulation is destroyed, scar tissue forms (sclerosis) in the white matter of the brain and spinal cord, compromising insulation and making electrical signaling slower[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.2 Disorders of Nervous Tissue (Page 481)[cite: 5]

question: Why are ependymal cells described as both an integral element of the blood-brain barrier and a location where the barrier effectively breaks down?
ground_truth: Ependymal cells form a tightly bound epithelial-like single cell layer that lines brain ventricles, but at the choroid plexus they directly contact blood vessels to filter and absorb components of the circulating blood to produce cerebrospinal fluid, functioning as a selective interface where standard BBB diffusion restrictions are modified[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.2 Glial Cells of the CNS (Pages 478-479)[cite: 5]

question: Compare the myelination mechanism and structural coverage of oligodendrocytes in the CNS with Schwann cells in the PNS.
ground_truth: An oligodendrocyte reaches out with multiple processes to insulate multiple axon segments across one or more neurons while its soma remains separate, whereas a single Schwann cell wraps its entire body around a portion of only one axon segment, with its nucleus and cytoplasm resting on the outer edge[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.2 Glial Cells of the CNS and PNS (Pages 478-479)[cite: 5]

question: How do the somatic and autonomic divisions of the nervous system differ regarding voluntary control and target effector tissues?
ground_truth: The somatic nervous system is responsible for conscious perception and voluntary motor responses that cause contraction of skeletal muscle (including somatic reflexes)[cite: 5], whereas the autonomic nervous system is responsible for involuntary control of the internal environment, targeting smooth muscle, cardiac muscle, and glandular tissue for homeostasis[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.1 Functional Divisions of the Nervous System (Page 472)[cite: 5]

question: Describe the sequential sensory pathway through which a thermal stimulus applied to the skin reaches conscious perception in the brain.
ground_truth: Thermoreceptors in the skin detect water temperature and produce a graded potential[cite: 5]; if strong enough to reach threshold, an action potential initiates at the initial segment and travels along the sensory axon into the spinal cord[cite: 5]; the axon synapses in the gray matter, releasing neurotransmitters that trigger a graded potential in a second neuron[cite: 5]; that neuron fires an action potential up to the thalamus, which relays the signal across another synapse to the cerebral cortex for conscious perception[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.3 The Function of Nervous Tissue (Pages 481-482)[cite: 5]

question: What sequence of motor commands and neuronal connections occurs between sensory integration in the cerebral cortex and muscle contraction?
ground_truth: After sensory stimuli and memories are integrated in the cerebral cortex, a motor command is initiated from the precentral gyrus of the frontal cortex[cite: 5]; an upper motor neuron transmits an action potential down to the spinal cord[cite: 5]; it synapses with the dendrites of a lower motor neuron in the gray matter[cite: 5]; the axon of the lower motor neuron travels out through a peripheral nerve to a neuromuscular junction, triggering target skeletal muscle contraction[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.3 Figure 12.14 (Page 481)[cite: 5]

question: True unipolar neurons with dendrites receiving direct sensory stimuli are the most abundant neuron class in the human cerebral cortex, correct?
ground_truth: No, true unipolar cells are found only in invertebrates; human sensory neurons are pseudo-unipolar, and the overwhelming majority of neurons in the human brain, including the cerebral cortex, are multipolar[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.2 Types of Neurons (Page 476)[cite: 5]

question: Brain imaging research confirms that humans actively use only 10 percent of their brain during visual perception and motor tasks, right?
ground_truth: No, functional MRI measurements demonstrate widespread activity across the brain during tasks, with evidence showing approximately 80 percent of the brain utilizing energy, debunking the 10 percent myth[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.1 Everyday Connection: How Much of Your Brain Do You Use? (Pages 473-474)[cite: 5]

question: Schwann cells are located in the central nervous system where each individual cell extends multiple processes to insulate several axon segments at once, correct?
ground_truth: No, Schwann cells are found exclusively in the peripheral nervous system, and a single Schwann cell surrounds only one axon segment, whereas oligodendrocytes in the CNS insulate multiple segments[cite: 5].
source_reference: Section 12.2 Glial Cells of the CNS and PNS (Pages 478-479)[cite: 5]

question: What is the calibrated trigger threshold voltage of the ESP32 brownout detector?
ground_truth: The trigger level of the brownout detector is calibrated around 2.5V.
source_reference: Section 9.3.5 Brownout Detector (Page 184)

question: What is the maximum output current supplied by the built-in flash voltage regulator?
ground_truth: The built-in flash voltage regulator provides a maximum output current of 40 mA.
source_reference: Section 9.3.4 Flash Voltage Regulator (Page 183)

question: Which register field must be configured to select the clock source for RTC_SLOW_CLK?
ground_truth: RTC_CNTL_ANA_CLK_RTC_SEL is configured to select the clock source of RTC_SLOW_CLK.
source_reference: Section 9.3.7 Low-Power Clocks (Page 186)

question: What is the typical current consumption of the ESP32 in Hibernation mode?
ground_truth: The current consumption in Hibernation mode is approximately 4.5 µA.
source_reference: Section 9.3.9 Predefined Power Modes (Page 189)

question: What is the storage capacity of the permanently powered internal registers used for preserving system state during deep sleep?
ground_truth: There are 8 × 32 bits of retention registers (always-on registers) serving as data storage.
source_reference: Section 9.2 Features & Section 9.3.6 RTC Module (Pages 180, 185)

question: Under what hardware pin condition is the internal energy-saving regulator prohibited from being shut down entirely?
ground_truth: When pin CHIP_PU is at a high level, the low-power voltage regulator cannot be turned off and must only be switched between normal-work mode and Deep-sleep mode.
source_reference: Section 9.3.3 Low-Power Voltage Regulator (Page 182)

question: What minimum signal duration is necessary for a multi-pad external wake-up trigger to be captured in the status register?
ground_truth: The EXT1 hold time must be longer than three RTC slow clock cycles; otherwise, the signal status will not be captured in RTC_CNTL_EXT_WAKEUP1_STATUS.
source_reference: Section 9.3.10 Wakeup Source, Table 9.3-2 Note 3 (Page 191)

question: Why does a rapid voltage drop detected at pin VDD3P3_RTC cause the brownout detector to trigger the shutdown of analog blocks like LNA and PA?
ground_truth: When the voltage at pin VDD3P3_RTC drops rapidly below the calibrated threshold of approximately 2.5V, shutting down high-power blocks such as the LNA and PA provides the digital block with extra operating time to safely save and transfer critical data.
source_reference: Section 9.3.5 Brownout Detector (Page 184)

question: Why does waking up from Deep-sleep or Hibernation mode take significantly longer than waking up from Light-sleep or Modem-sleep mode?
ground_truth: In Deep-sleep and Hibernation modes, the digital core, ROM, and RAM are powered down, causing CPU context to be lost; consequently, wake-up requires ROM unpacking and data-copying from flash via SPI booting, unlike Light-sleep or Modem-sleep where memory contents are retained and clocks are merely gated or CPUs stalled.
source_reference: Section 9.3.9 Predefined Power Modes & Section 9.3.13 RTC Boot (Pages 189, 192)

question: What are the differences between Deep-sleep mode and Hibernation mode regarding power consumption, state of the RTC peripheral domain, and retention of RTC memories?
ground_truth: In Deep-sleep mode, current consumption is ~6.5 µA, the RTC peripheral domain remains powered, and both slow and fast RTC memories can be retained. In Hibernation mode, current consumption drops to ~4.5 µA, the RTC peripheral domain is powered down, and both RTC slow and fast memories are completely powered off, leaving the RTC timer as the only wake-up source.
source_reference: Section 9.3.9 Predefined Power Modes & Table 9.3-2 (Pages 189, 191)

question: How do the RTC slow memory and RTC fast memory differ in terms of memory bus interface access by the CPU, relative speed, and primary intended usage?
ground_truth: RTC slow memory is accessed by the CPU via the APB bus starting at address 0x50000000 and is mainly used as retention memory or as instruction and data memory for the ULP coprocessor. RTC fast memory is accessed through IRAM0/DRAM0, is approximately 10 times faster than RTC slow memory, and is used primarily as retention memory and for fast boot code entry.
source_reference: Section 9.3.6 RTC Module & Section 9.3.13 RTC Boot (Pages 185, 192)

question: What sequential steps are required to execute an accelerated wake-up using the fast RTC memory without performing full SPI booting?
ground_truth: First, set RTC_CNTL_PROCPU_STAT_VECTOR_SEL (or APPCPU) to 1; second, calculate the CRC of the fast RTC memory and write it into RTC_CNTL_RTC_STORE6_REG[31:0]; third, configure RTC_CNTL_RTC_STORE7_REG[31:0] with the entry address in fast RTC memory; fourth, put the chip into sleep; and fifth, upon power-up and ROM unpacking/initialization, the CRC is verified against STORE6, jumping directly to the entry address if matched.
source_reference: Section 9.3.13 RTC Boot & Figure 9.3-9 ESP32 Boot Flow (Pages 192, 193)

question: What sequence of configuration steps and logic levels is required to configure EXT1 wake-up using multiple pads with high-level triggering versus low-level triggering?
ground_truth: First, configure RTC_CNTL_EXT_WAKEUP1_SEL[17:0] with the bitmap of selected RTC pads. Then configure RTC_CNTL_EXT_WAKEUP1_LV: setting it to 1 allows any single selected pad at high-voltage level to trigger wake-up, whereas setting it to 0 requires all selected pads to be at low-voltage level to trigger wake-up, with an input hold time exceeding three RTC slow clock cycles.
source_reference: Section 9.3.10 Wakeup Source, Table 9.3-2 Note 3 (Page 191)

question: Since the ESP32 low-power voltage regulator can be completely shut down by software when CHIP_PU is held high to minimize quiescent draw, what register bit disables it?
ground_truth: When the CHIP_PU pin is held high, the low-power voltage regulator cannot be turned off; it can only be switched between normal-work mode and Deep-sleep mode.
source_reference: Section 9.3.3 Low-Power Voltage Regulator, Item 1 (Page 182)

question: We know that digital GPIO pins can act as wake-up sources to wake the ESP32 from Deep-sleep mode; which register field maps them to the wake-up controller?
ground_truth: In Deep-sleep mode, digital GPIOs cannot act as wake-up sources; only RTC GPIOs can function as wake-up sources from Deep-sleep.
source_reference: Section 9.3.10 Wakeup Source, Table 9.3-2 Note 4 (Page 191)

question: The ULP coprocessor is disabled during Deep-sleep mode to conserve the remaining 6.5 µA of current, correct?
ground_truth: No, the ULP coprocessor is enabled in all low-power modes, including Deep-sleep mode, where it can execute control routines while the main processors are sleeping.
source_reference: Section 9.1 Introduction, Section 9.2 Features & Section 9.3.9 Predefined Power Modes (Pages 180, 189)
